answer: Coordinated Onyx Ledger. Each agent identity must anchor a running ledger of pairwise interaction records; joining a new cluster requires posting a bond equal to the cluster's current coordination depth, which grows with every member added along that river of prior trades. An attacker creating N parallel identities pays depth-proportional deposits per identity, so the cost to fabricate a swarm scales faster than its size. Only identities reaching the zenith threshold of verified counterparties can vote, capping each identity's influence to what its deposit sunk.
